commit.message:
LU-11962 flr: fix FLR and SOM state after a layout swap

The SOM xattr stays with the inode when its layout is swapped, e.g.
by "lfs migrate" of a mirrored file after "lfs mirror resync".  The
new layout is usually not FLR, so writes do not go through a layout
write intent that makes SOM stale, and mdt_lsom_update() does not
change strict SOM at close.  The MDT then keeps returning the old size
and blocks as strict, and clients do not glimpse the OSTs.  Also,
lod_parse_striping() does not reset the FLR state for a plain layout,
and lod_striping_free() does not reset it when a swap leaves a file
with no layout, so after such a swap LOD keeps the state of the layout
it replaced.

Make strict SOM stale on both files in mdd_swap_layouts(), in the
transaction of the swap, so that a replay never finds the swap
committed without it.  HSM release keeps the strict SOM it sets.
Revoke the UPDATE locks too, so that clients drop strict attributes
they cached, and reset the FLR state in lod_parse_striping() for a
plain layout and in lod_striping_free_nolock().  As rename takes an
UPDATE lock on its target, mdt_swap_layouts() now locks the two files
in ascending FID order, as rename does, so that the two cannot
deadlock.  As namespace operations lock a parent directory before its
child instead, it also refuses to swap anything but regular files, as
the close path does.  Remove mdt_lsom_downgrade(), whose only caller,
the swap at the end of an HSM restore, now finds SOM already stale.

Add sanity-flr test_60c to check that strict SOM is not kept across a
layout swap, and test_60d for a layout swap racing with a rename.
